spans.s:
लिप्सा, f. (fr. the Desid.), the desire to gain, wish
to acquire or obtain, desire for possessing.

लिप्सा लिप्सा, लिप्सु, लिप्स्य, &c. See p. 862,
col. 1.

लिप्सित, अस्, आ, अम्, wished to be obtained,
coveted, desired.

लिप्सितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, desirable to be obtained,
to be wished for.

लीप्सितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. worthy of being
acquired, desirable.

लिप्सु, उस्, उस्, उ, wishing to gain or obtain, de-
siring to become possessed of (with acc.), eager for,
desirous of, covetous.
—लिप्सु-ता, f. the state of
wishing to obtain, covetousness.

लिप्स्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be wished to be obtained,
desirable to be acquired, eligible.

लिप् लिप् (the later and classical form
of rt. रिप्), cl. 6. P. A. लिम्पति, -ते,
लिलेप, लिलिपे, लेप्स्यति, -ते, अलिपत्, अलिपत or
अलिप्त, लेप्तुम्, to smear, besmear, anoint, daub,
plaster, paint; to spread over, cover; to stain, soil,
pollute, defile, contaminate; to inflame, kindle,
burn: Pass. लिप्यते, to be smeared or anointed; to
stick, cleave, adhere to: Caus. लेपयति, -यितुम्,
Aor. अलीलिपत्, to cause to smear, &c.; to smear,
anoint, cover; to cause to be covered or decorated:
Desid. लिलिप्सति, -ते: Intens. लेलिप्यते, लेलेप्ति;
[]
[cf. Gr. λίπ-α, λίπ-ος, λιπαρό-ς, λιπ-αρ-ής, λιπαρ-έ-ω,
ἀ-λείφ-ω, ἄλειφ-αρ, ἄλειφα, λισσός: Lat.
limpidus, lippus, li-no, li-mus, de-libuo; probably
also liquidus, liqueo: Old Germ. salba: Goth.
salbôn: Angl. Sax. sealf: Slav. lep-i-ti, lep-u:
Lith. limp-u, lip-ti, lip-u-s: Hib. laib, laibe,
‘mire, clay.’]
लिप, अस्, m. smearing, anointing, plastering.

लिपि, इस्, or लिपी, f. smearing, besmearing, anoint-
ing, plastering, spreading over; painting, drawing;
writing, transcribing, handwriting; the art of writing;
written characters, the letters; a writing, written
paper or book, manuscript, document, letter.
—लिपि-
कर, अस्, m. an anointer, white-washer, plasterer;
a writer, scribe; an engraver.
—लिपि-कार, अस्, m. a
writer, scribe, copyist.
—लिपि-ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, one who
understands writing, one who can write.
—लिपि-
न्यास, अस्, m. ‘the act of putting down written
characters, ‘writing, transcribing.
—लिपि-फलक,
अम्, n. a writing-tablet, leaf for writing on.
—लिपि-
शाला, f. a writing-school.
—लिपि-सङ्ख्या, f. a
number of written characters.
—लिपि-सज्जा, f. imple-
ments or materials for writing.
लिपिका, f. = लिपि, a writing, written paper, &c.

1. लिप्त, अस्, आ, अम् (for 2. लिप्त see p. 868, col. 1),
smeared, besmeared, anointed; stained, soiled, de-
filed; smeared with poison, poisoned, envenomed;
eaten.
—लिप्त-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, one who has smeared
or anointed, &c.
—लिप्त-हस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, having
the hands smeared or stained.
—लिप्ताङ्ग (˚त-अङ्˚),
अस्, आ or ई, अम्, having the body anointed with
unguents, &c.

लिप्त 2. लिप्त, अस्, आ, अम् (according to
Uṇādi-s.

. fr. rt. 1. ली; for 1. लिप्त see p. 867,
col. 3), united, joined, connected, embraced.

लिप्ता लिप्ता or लिप्तिका, f. a minute, the
sixtieth part of a degree; [cf. Gr. λεπτός.]
—लिप्ती-
कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., Ved. to reduce to minutes.

लिप्तक, अस्, आ, अम्, smeared, covered with poison;
(अस्), m. a poisoned arrow.
